But I never had a booking confirmation or any reminder, so the slot simply slipped my mind. When I realised and rang to cancel, I sat in the call-queue for ages, got a call-back after the time had passed, and the appointment was wasted.

It’s frustrating because this could be fixed so easily:
•	Send an SMS or e-mail confirmation the moment the slot is booked.
•	Follow it with a quick reminder the day before, with a one-tap “cancel/re-book” link. Trials at other trusts show simple texts cut missed appointments by up to 40 %.
•	Make sure the phone system lets patients cancel quickly without weaving through endless menus or long hold times.

Each missed GP slot costs the NHS about £40 and denies someone else care. I’d much rather the money – and the clinician’s time – went to a patient who can attend.

The staff here are polite and professional when you finally get through, but the digital side badly needs attention.
